title: Leviticus Bible Quiz - Chapter 23
description: Ten questions on Leviticus 23: the set feasts of Yahweh, from Passover and the first fruits to the day of atonement and the feast of booths.

questions.text: When is Yahweh's Passover, according to verse 5?
questions.explanation: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month in the evening, is Yahweh's Passover.

answers.text: The fifteenth day of the seventh month
The fourteenth day of the first month, in the evening
The tenth day of the seventh month
The first day of the seventh month

questions.text: What were the Israelites to bring to the priest when they reaped the harvest in the land?
questions.explanation: They were to bring the sheaf of the first fruits of their harvest to the priest, who would wave it before Yahweh.

answers.text: A tenth of all the grain of their fields
A basket of figs and grapes from the vines
A jar of beaten olive oil for the lamp
The sheaf of the first fruits of their harvest

questions.text: What were they not allowed to eat until they had brought this offering to God?
questions.explanation: Verse 14 says they must not eat bread, roasted grain or fresh grain until they had brought the offering of their God.

answers.text: Bread, roasted grain or fresh grain
Meat from their herds and flocks
Honey, figs or dates
Fish caught in the rivers

questions.text: After the seventh Sabbath, how many days were they to count before offering a new meal offering?
questions.explanation: The next day after the seventh Sabbath they were to count fifty days and offer a new meal offering to Yahweh.

answers.text: Forty days
Seventy days
Fifty days
Thirty days

questions.text: How were the two loaves for the wave offering to be baked?
questions.explanation: The two loaves of fine flour were to be baked with yeast, as first fruits to Yahweh.

answers.text: Without yeast
With yeast
With honey
On hot stones

questions.text: What was held on the first day of the seventh month?
questions.explanation: On the first day of the seventh month there was a solemn rest, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, a holy convocation.

answers.text: A memorial of blowing of trumpets
The feast of booths
The feast of unleavened bread
The wave offering of the sheaf

questions.text: On which day was the day of atonement?
questions.explanation: Verse 27 says the day of atonement is on the tenth day of the seventh month.

answers.text: The first day of the first month
The fifteenth day of the seventh month
The fourteenth day of the seventh month
The tenth day of the seventh month

questions.text: What would happen to anyone who did not deny himself on the day of atonement?
questions.explanation: Verse 29 says whoever does not deny himself on that day shall be cut off from his people.

answers.text: He would have to pay a fine
He would have to offer a double sacrifice
He would be cut off from his people
He would be unclean until evening

questions.text: Which of these were they to take on the first day of the feast of booths?
questions.explanation: They were to take the fruit of majestic trees, branches of palm trees, boughs of thick trees and willows of the brook, and rejoice before Yahweh seven days.

answers.text: Willows of the brook
Cedar wood and hyssop
Ears of barley
Branches of the fig tree

questions.text: Why were all native-born Israelites to dwell in temporary shelters for seven days?
questions.explanation: They were to do this so that their generations would know that Yahweh made Israel dwell in temporary shelters when he brought them out of Egypt.

answers.text: To remember the tents of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
So later generations would know Israel lived in shelters after Egypt
Because the harvest fields were far away from their homes
To honor the priests who lived at the Tent of Meeting
